newsitem.title: UK: Britain sells RfD rail freight to EWS.
newsitem.headline: Britain sells RfD rail freight to EWS.

text.p: Britain's Department of Transport said on Thursday it had agreed the privatisation sale of British Rail's Channel Tunnel freight business Railfreight Distribution (RfD) to the English Welsh and Scottish Railway (EWS) consortium.

EWS, part-owned by Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp of the United States, is the dominant operator of British rail freight companies and already controls three bulk cargo firms and a national mail and parcels business.

No financial details of the sale were disclosed but the government had already announced in January that it would have no objections on monopolies grounds if EWS were to be chosen as the preferred buyer for RfD.
The sale would, however, have to be cleared by the European Commission prior to completion, the ministry said.

Transport Minister Sir George Young said the sale would help stimulate more international transport of goods by rail. "RfD will now have the freedom and incentive to build on the opportunities created by the Channel Tunnel to get more international freight on rail -- good news not only for the business, but also for its customers and the environment," he said.

If EWS can successfully increase the volume of freight using the RfD services through the tunnel it could also bring revenue benefits for its Anglo-French operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc, as well as the London & Continental consortium planning to build a high-speed link between the tunnel's northern entrance and London.
Young said the experience of EWS during its initial stewardship of the bulk and parcel freight sectors had underpinned the decision to sell RfD to the operator.
"EWS have already demonstrated their determination to win domestic business from road haulage by offering customers first class service and keen prices."
The sale will leave Britain with just one other significant rail-borne freight operator -- container specialist Freightliner, which is owned by a venture capital-backed management group.
Industry sources had said Freightlines had also expressed an interest in buying RfD in conjunction with rail and bus passenger operator Stagecoach Holdings Plc.
